A close watch should also be kept on the patient’s state of hy- dration since fluid overload is considered to be a key risk factor for pulmonary oedema. The infusion should be continued for 12 to 48 hours after the contractions have stopped. Ritodrine hydrochloride may subse- quently be given by mouth in an initial dose of 10 mg every 2 hours for 24 hours, starting 30 minutes before the end of the intravenous infusion. Thereafter, 10 to 20 mg may be given every 4 to 6 hours according to the patient’s response. The total daily oral dose should not exceed 120 mg. If intravenous infusion is inappropriate, 10 mg may be given intramuscularly every 3 to 8 hours and contin- ued for 12 to 48 hours after the contractions have stopped. ◊ Reviews. 1.
